records.title: no credentials shows the required-field error
records.acText: With both fields empty, an error banner reads 'Epic sadface: Username is required'.

records.title: missing password shows the required-field error
records.acText: With a username but no password, an error banner reads 'Epic sadface: Password is required'.

records.title: missing username shows the required-field error
records.acText: With a password but no username, an error banner reads 'Epic sadface: Username is required'.

records.title: invalid credentials are rejected
records.acText: Invalid credentials are rejected with 'Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service'.

records.title: locked_out_user is rejected with the lockout error
records.acText: locked_out_user submitting the correct password (secret_sauce) on the login page is not authenticated — the browser stays on the login page and never reaches /inventory.html — and sees the error banner with the exact text "Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out."

records.title: locked_out_user with a wrong password sees the credentials error, not the lockout error
records.acText: locked_out_user submitting an incorrect password on the login page sees the invalid-credentials error — "Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service" — and not the lockout error. The credential check takes precedence over the account's locked state, so the lockout is never revealed to someone who does not hold the password.
